QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_8

question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund is close-ended, 6-year tenure + 2-year extension used. Its Liquidation Period (Reg 29(9A)) of 1 year is also ending. Unliquidated investments remain at 18% of NAV. The Manager proposes entering a Dissolution Period. What investor consent is needed for the Dissolution Period itself?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Regulation 29 read with the SEBI circular dated 26-April-2024, entering the Dissolution Period requires approval of at least 75% of investors BY VALUE of their investment in the existing AIF scheme. This is the same threshold as for in-specie distribution during the Liquidation Period. The Trap: Two-thirds (option B) is the tenure-EXTENSION threshold — different provision. Simple majority (option A) is a generic corporate threshold and does not apply. Unanimity never applies to AIF governance. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) covers the same Dissolution Period framework introduced via the 2024 SEBI amendment. XIX-C tests both tracks. XIX-E focuses on Cat III application. Manager's Pro-Tip: Prepare the Information Memorandum + merchant-banker Due Diligence Certificate well before the Liquidation Period expires — the filing MUST be made before expiry. Miss the window and mandatory in-specie-at-Re.1 is triggered, hurting the manager's track record.
